page: Google Cloud Platform m4-megamem-28 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the m4 server family. It is configured with 28 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 CPU architecture and features 372.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a high memory-to-core ratio of 13.29 GB per vCPU, designed specifically for memory-intensive workloads.

This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. There are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density position this instance as a specialized resource where the resource density is optimized for massive RAM capacity relative to the compute footprint.

The m4-megamem-28 is engineered for workloads requiring large in-memory datasets. Appropriate use cases include large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, real-time data analytics, and memory-heavy caching layers where high RAM capacity is critical and local storage is not a prerequisite.
